title: HyperEF 2.0: Spectral Hypergraph Coarsening via Krylov Subspace Expansion and Resistance-Based Local Clustering
problem: Hypergraph partitioning and coarsening require preserving structural properties while maintaining solution quality. Existing methods struggle to balance coarsening effectiveness with solution quality metrics like conductance.
motivation: Efficient, high-quality hypergraph partitioning is critical for VLSI physical design and circuit optimization at scale.
method: HyperEF 2.0 coarsens hypergraphs (groups of densely interconnected nodes) by measuring node distances through an expanded mathematical search space — specifically, Krylov subspace expansion using both clique and star connection patterns — to better estimate 'effective resistance' (the structural distance between nodes). It then groups nearby nodes together using this resistance metric (resistance-based local clustering), merging them into larger supergroups while keeping the partition balanced. Finally, it integrates this process into multilevel partitioning, recursively coarsening at multiple scales while adjusting hyperedge weights and applying community detection to maintain solution quality.
key_novelty: The key innovation is using an expanded mathematical search space (Krylov subspace expansion with clique and star patterns) to measure node distances more accurately as 'effective resistance,' then grouping nodes based on this resistance metric to simplify hypergraphs while maintaining solution balance.
contributions: Expanded Krylov subspace approach improving effective resistance approximation
Resistance-based local clustering for better cluster balance
State-of-the-art performance on VLSI hypergraph benchmarks
Up to 4.5× speedup over prior flow-based clustering methods
limitations: Evaluation limited to VLSI benchmarks; generalization to other hypergraph applications unclear.
primary_theme: Efficient spectral hypergraph partitioning for VLSI
